page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.d1.4xlarge is a storage-focused instance designed for massive local disk capacity workloads. Powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64 GB of system RAM, establishing a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Crucially, the instance comes bundled with 47,244 GB of local HDD storage and provides a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth virtualized on a KVM hypervisor.

The primary architectural advantage of the ecs.d1.4xlarge lies in its high local HDD storage density. Providing over 47 TB of attached spinning disk capacity, it offers significant resource density per compute node, making it cost-effective for big data ingestion and sequential disk logging. However, because local storage relies on magnetic hard drives rather than NVMe SSDs, random read and write IOPS performance is lower compared to solid-state configurations. Advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 are also not supported on this CPU generation.

Due to its heavy local HDD storage capacity, the ecs.d1.4xlarge is suitable for distributed file systems such as Apache Hadoop, MapReduce cluster nodes, central log accumulation repositories, and data archival pipelines where massive sequential throughput outweighs low-latency random access requirements.

The primary differentiator of this server is its bundled 47,244 GB local HDD array, offering substantial storage capacity for data-intensive processing. While the high magnetic disk capacity delivers cost efficiency for bulk storage workloads, the use of spinning hard drives presents lower random IOPS performance compared to solid-state drives. Benchmark measurements are currently unavailable for this hardware profile. The instance provides an optimal operational fit for distributed big data processing, Apache Hadoop nodes, log collection pipelines, and large scale sequential storage systems where bulk disk capacity takes precedence over low-latency random access.
